answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should tie each identity to a costly, verifiable history. A public beacon publishes periodic randomness agents must anchor work to, so one operator cannot cheaply replay the same proof across thousands of clones. Each identity must stake a scarce resource and earn attestations over time, like a jade seal gaining weight only after sustained honest service; newcomers start weak. Attackers must then buy many distinct histories, costing more than any single fraud gains, while quartz-clear audit trails let peers revoke clones whose records contradict each other.
